scope: Native SmartAI waypoint-action failure exposed by Vereesa's stage-5 Inquisitor approach. Shared action repair, not a replacement movement system or full artifact-chain certification.

findings.before: SmartScript::ProcessAction sets runOnce before dispatch. WP_START calls void SmartAI::StartPath, then unconditionally configures the escort quest/despawn and executes its LINK. StartPath rejects combat, missing/empty paths and a missing next point without reporting failure. Vereesa100397 event30 therefore consumed its NOT_REPEATABLE DATA9/9 and ran LINK31/33 dialogue/conversation even when no MovePoint was issued. Qormaladon101269 still sent every second, but those later signals could not recover the consumed event.
findings.native_constraints: The native combat prohibition remains intact. No speculative OOC condition, forced evade/combat stop, teleport, fabricated waypoint, invulnerability or progress grant was added. Successful path starts must still issue the real MovePoint and native WAYPOINT_START callback. Motion request acceptance does not establish navigation completion or visible client movement.
findings.repair: StartPath now returns false for the native rejection branches and true only after MovePoint and WAYPOINT_START. WP_START restores runOnce=false and returns before escort quest/despawn configuration or dependent LINK when rejected. On a later real DATA9/9 signal, Vereesa can retry under the existing972/5 condition; successful/reentrant/repeated signals retain native one-shot consumption. Escort targets and react-state setup retain their original ordering before StartPath; this is not a rollback of every preparatory action.
findings.first_point: GetNextWayPoint now resolves before arming SMART_ESCORT_ESCORTING. A missing first point resets the cursor and returns false without creating an escort with null mLastWP, avoiding a subsequent retry entering StopPath with that invalid state. Existing loader gap diagnostics and combat diagnostic remain enabled. Successful waypoint order, run/repeat settings, last-OOC pose and callback order remain unchanged.
